Some pictures from last years trip to Laos.

Last year I was 6/7 weeks in Laos and Thailand with a friend of mine.

If you have any questions, feel free to ask!

Thanks so much for sharing the photos. Laos looks really gorgeous! Were there any cities in the country that you preferred to others? Any 'must see' destinations that were actually 'meh'? I always like to hear from people who have visited places, rather than relying on the wisdom of WikiVoyage or travel guides. :)

I only spend 3 weeks in Laos, so I only visited a small part of the country, mainly the northwest, the most known citys Vientiane, Vang Vieng, Luang Prabang and Houay Xai, a bordertown to Thailand. So I can only tell you about those few and not about the northeast and the whole south, which I heard is really amazing.

We started in Vientiane, got to Vang Vieng, then Luang Prabang and after a 2 day Mekong boat tour we stayed a few days in Houay Xai, after that we left for Thailand. Vientiane is the capital of Laos, and the biggest city. You can see a lot of wats (temples), a few museums and monuments, and the Buddha-Park you see in one photo. The city is nothing special, but it was nice to accustom to the Lao-lifestyle.

Vang Vieng, as most people will probably tell you, is IMO awful, were it not for its surroundings. It is a small village without anything to do or watch except for renting motorcycles or bicycles and go to the caves, Lagoons or simply take in the beautiful scenery. The village itself has nothing to offer, except watching Friends or drinking. I would say skip Vang Vieng, but its surroundings are really beautiful.

Luang Prabang is the backpacker hub. It is known for its many wats (temples) and monks, probably most popular for the alms ceremony. It is the fourth biggest city in Laos and the old capital of the Kingdom Laos. There is the old palace and, as I already said, a lot of wats.

Houay Xai is a little bordertown at the border to Thailand. Most of the backpacker only know it because it is a transit town to/from Thailand. It has not a lot to offer for tourists, and almost everyone leaves after one night. That´s what made it nice IMO, because there where almost no other people except for us, and nobody tried to get our money.

The northeast and south of Laos are, from what I was told, really beautiful and I really should have visited them as well, but I hadn´t enough time. All in all, Laos has a relly beautiful scenery, really nice people and is really cheap. I can not recommend visiting it enough.
The beauty of that country, It Never End...
Yeah it was really really beautiful. I thought it was much more beautiful than Thailand!
